label: World Register of Marine Species (WoRMS) REST API (Aphia records)
governance: Governed international taxonomic infrastructure hosted by the Flanders Marine Institute (VLIZ). about.php describes three levels: an elected Steering Committee, the Editorial Board (taxonomic editors responsible for their groups) and the Data Management Team. Data are licensed CC BY 4.0 (about.php: 'Creative Commons Attribution License (CC-BY)'; images CC BY-NC-SA). The database has a DataCite DOI, 10.14284/170 ('World Register of Marine Species. Available from https://www.marinespecies.org at VLIZ. Accessed yyyy-mm-dd'), and a peer-reviewed description (Costello et al. 2013, PLoS ONE 8:e51629). All checked 2026-10-31.
versioning: Live, continuously edited database; the citation convention is DOI plus access date. Each Aphia record carries a 'modified' timestamp and a stable AphiaID; records are not deleted but marked unaccepted/deleted with a valid_AphiaID pointer. Query responses (AphiaRecordByAphiaID, AphiaRecordsByName, AphiaIDByName) are deterministic JSON for a given state, so byte checksums are reproducible until a record is edited.
known_issues: Name queries for non-marine or unregistered taxa return HTTP 204 (no content); vendored records store such distributions without a checksum, which is correct but leaves nothing to verify.
Because the register is live, a record edit changes the response bytes; 415 of 415 recorded response checksums still matched on 2026-10-31, so drift is slow but not zero.
WoRMS aggregates regional and taxon-specific registers (e.g. ERMS) and shares editors with them; it is also a source for GBIF and Open Tree, which are vendored separately in this project.
rationale: WoRMS is the archetype of the rubric's 1.0 anchor for authority: a governed international infrastructure with editorial board, DOI, documented API and licence. Records are curated primary nomenclatural data, independent of this project; the 0.9 reflects that WoRMS content is itself ingested by other vendored sources (GBIF backbone, Open Tree), so cross-source agreement is not fully independent evidence. Every URL and DOI listed resolves and the API re-queries reproduced the vendored AphiaIDs, names and ranks.
